answer: In a decentralized network, a Sybil-resistant mechanism utilizes a proof-of-stake system tied to a unique, hardware-rooted identity. Each agent is assigned a "copper stake" - a scarce, transferable token linked to a physical device. When an agent attempts to participate, it must echo a challenge to prove possession of the stake. An attacker attempting to create multiple identities would need to establish a separate, costly inlet for each fake identity, making large-scale Sybil attacks economically infeasible due to the high cost of acquiring and maintaining multiple stakes.
